title: Messages and voicemails
goal: Understand short phone messages and texts, catch names, numbers and times, and leave a simple voicemail.

items.fr: C'est de la part de qui ?

items.note: On the phone, say c'est + your name, not je suis.

items.fr: Je vous appelle pour mon rendez-vous.
accept: Je vous appelle pour mon rendez-vous
Pouvez-vous me rappeler, s'il vous plaît ?
Pouvez-vous me rappeler s'il vous plaît ?

example.fr: J'ai un message vocal de la clinique.
example.en: I have a voicemail from the clinic.

items.note: In France: À tout à l'heure !

blocks.title: A voicemail from a clinic
blocks.context: Amira finds this message on her phone. Who is calling, and why?
blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Nathalie Gagnon, de la clinique Saint-Laurent. Je vous appelle pour votre rendez-vous de jeudi. Le docteur Roy n'est pas disponible à dix heures. Est-ce que c'est possible à quatorze heures ? Rappelez-moi au cinq, un, quatre, cinq, cinq, cinq, zéro, un, neuf, huit. Merci, bonne journée !
blocks.en: Hello, this is Nathalie Gagnon from the Saint-Laurent clinic. I'm calling about your appointment on Thursday. Dr. Roy isn't available at ten o'clock. Is two p.m. possible? Call me back at 514 555 0198. Thank you, have a nice day!

blocks.title: A voicemail from a friend
blocks.context: Then a second message, from Sofia.
blocks.fr: Salut Amira, c'est Sofia ! Ce soir, on va au cinéma avec Karim. Tu veux venir avec nous ? Le film commence à vingt heures trente. Envoie-moi un texto ! Bisous !
blocks.en: Hi Amira, it's Sofia! Tonight we're going to the movies with Karim. Do you want to come with us? The film starts at 8:30 p.m. Send me a text! Love!

blocks.title: Two text messages
blocks.fr:
Olivier : Salut Mei ! Désolé, je vais être en retard. J'arrive à 19 h 15, devant le restaurant. À tantôt !
Mei : Pas de problème, c'est correct ! Karim et moi, on est déjà là.
blocks.en:
Olivier: Hi Mei! Sorry, I'm going to be late. I'll be there at 7:15 p.m., in front of the restaurant. See you soon!
Mei: No problem, that's fine! Karim and I are already here.

blocks.body: For each message, listen for four things only: **who** is calling, **why**, **when** (day and time) and **which number** to call back.

blocks.title: On the phone
blocks.body:
- Answer with [[Allô ?]] (in France, *allô* is only for the phone) or with the name of the place: [[Clinique Saint-Laurent, bonjour !]]
- Say who you are with [[c'est…]]: [[Bonjour, c'est Raj Patel.]] On the phone, *je suis* sounds strange.
- If someone asks [[C'est de la part de qui ?]] (Who's calling?), just give your name: [[Raj Patel.]] or [[C'est Raj Patel.]]
- [[Un instant, s'il vous plaît.]] = One moment, please.
- [[Elle n'est pas là.]] = She isn't here. [[Vous voulez laisser un message ?]] = Would you like to leave a message?

blocks.title: Leaving a voicemail
blocks.pattern: Bonjour, c'est… · Je vous appelle pour… · Rappelez-moi au… · Merci, bonne journée !
blocks.note: After [[Je vous appelle pour]], use a **noun** ([[pour mon rendez-vous]]) or an **infinitive** ([[pour confirmer]] = to confirm). Give your number after [[au]]: [[Rappelez-moi au 613 555 0147.]]

examples.fr: Je vous appelle pour confirmer mon rendez-vous.
examples.en: I'm calling to confirm my appointment.

blocks.title: Formal or friendly?
head: formal (vous)
friendly (tu)
blocks.note: [[Bisous]] (kisses) is a friendly goodbye between friends and family, in messages or on the phone. Never use it with a clinic or a boss!

blocks.title: Catching the key details
blocks.body:
Real messages are fast, but the important information is always the same:

- **Names:** often spelled out. Remember the alphabet: [[G-A-G-N-O-N]].
- **Times:** official messages use the 24-hour clock: [[quatorze heures]] = 2 p.m., [[vingt heures trente]] = 8:30 p.m.
- **Days:** [[lundi, mardi, jeudi…]] Listen for [[de]]: [[votre rendez-vous de jeudi]] = your Thursday appointment.
- **Phone numbers:** in Canada, 10 digits: the area code ([[514]], [[613]], [[819]]…) then 7 digits.

If you miss something, you can listen to a voicemail again. On a live call, ask: [[Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?]]

blocks.title: Words and phrases in this lesson

blocks.body:
- **c'est, not je suis:** [[Bonjour, c'est Mei.]] On the phone, *Je suis Mei* sounds odd.
- **appeler vs rappeler:** [[Appelez-moi]] = call me; [[Rappelez-moi]] = call me **back**.
- **appeler has two l's** in *je, tu, il, ils*: [[j'appelle]], [[ils appellent]], but [[nous appelons]], [[vous appelez]]. You know this already from [[je m'appelle]].
- **au + number:** [[Rappelez-moi au 514…]], not *à 514*.
- **pour + noun or infinitive:** [[pour mon rendez-vous]], [[pour confirmer]].

- In Québec, [[Allô !]] is also a friendly **hello in person**: [[Allô, ça va ?]] In France it's only for the phone.
- A text message is a [[texto]] (you'll also hear [[un texte]] in Québec; in France people also say [[un SMS]]). [[Texter]] = to text.
- Your voicemail box is your [[boîte vocale]]: [[Laissez un message dans ma boîte vocale.]]
- [[À tantôt !]] = see you later today. In France: [[À tout à l'heure !]]
- Many Quebecers also say [[Bye !]] at the end of a call.

examples.en: Hi Sofia! How are you? (Québec, in person)

blocks.title: Saying phone numbers
blocks.body:
In **Canada**, many people say a phone number digit by digit: [[cinq, un, quatre — cinq, cinq, cinq — zéro, un, neuf, huit]]. Some group the last four digits in pairs: [[zéro un, quatre-vingt-dix-huit]].

In **France**, numbers have 10 digits starting with 0 and are usually said in pairs: [[06 12 34 56 78]] = [[zéro six, douze, trente-quatre, cinquante-six, soixante-dix-huit]]. Practise your numbers to 99 for this!

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.en: Hello, this is Raj Patel. I'm calling about my appointment.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. You can replay each message as many times as you need.

blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Karim Haddad. Je vous appelle pour l'appartement. Rappelez-moi au six, un, trois, cinq, cinq, cinq, zéro, un, quatre, sept. Merci !
blocks.en: Hello, this is Karim Haddad. I'm calling about the apartment. Call me back at 613 555 0147. Thanks!
blocks.prompt: Which number should you call back?
blocks.explain: Six, un, trois… zéro, un, quatre, sept: 613 555 0147.

blocks.fr: Salut, c'est Mei ! Le cours de français ne commence pas à dix-huit heures, mais à dix-neuf heures. À tantôt !
blocks.en: Hi, it's Mei! The French class doesn't start at 6 p.m. but at 7 p.m. See you later!
blocks.prompt: What time does the class start?
blocks.explain: [[ne… pas à dix-huit heures, mais à dix-neuf heures]]: not 18:00 but 19:00.

blocks.fr: Bonjour, ici la pharmacie du Centre. Vos médicaments sont prêts. Vous pouvez passer demain, après dix heures.
blocks.en: Hello, this is the Centre pharmacy. Your medication is ready. You can come by tomorrow, after ten o'clock.
blocks.explain: [[Vos médicaments sont prêts]] = your medication is ready. [[ici]] is another way to say who is calling: [[ici la pharmacie]].

blocks.text: Bonjour, ___ Raj Patel. Je vous ___ pour mon rendez-vous. ___-moi au 613 555 0147.
blocks.en: Hello, this is Raj Patel. I'm calling about my appointment. Call me back at 613 555 0147.
blocks.explain: c'est + name; je vous appelle (two l's); Rappelez-moi = call me back (formal).

blocks.prompt: The receptionist asks: “C'est de la part de qui ?” What do you answer?
optionFeedback: She wants to know who is calling, not where you are.
That's what the receptionist says, not the caller.
She's asking who you are, not when.

blocks.prompt: Leave a voicemail for a dentist's office. Say who you are, why you're calling (you can't come to your appointment), suggest another day, and give your number.
checklist: Je ne peux pas… / Est-ce que c'est possible… ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour, c'est Sofia Ramírez. Je vous appelle pour mon rendez-vous de mardi à neuf heures. Je ne peux pas être là, parce que je dois travailler. Est-ce que c'est possible jeudi après-midi ? Rappelez-moi au 819 555 0142, s'il vous plaît. Merci, bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, this is Sofia Ramírez. I'm calling about my appointment on Tuesday at nine. I can't be there, because I have to work. Is Thursday afternoon possible? Please call me back at 819 555 0142. Thank you, have a nice day!

blocks.prompt: Reply by text to Sofia's voicemail about the cinema. Say yes, say you're going to be a little late and give a time, and ask one question.
checklist: Je vais être en retard + a time

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Sofia ! Oui, je veux bien ! Mais je vais être un peu en retard : j'arrive à 20 h 20. Le cinéma est où ? À tantôt !
models.en: Hi Sofia! Yes, I'd love to! But I'm going to be a little late: I'll get there at 8:20. Where is the cinema? See you later!

summary:
- Pick out who, why, when and which number in a short voicemail or text
- Handle a call: [[Allô ?]] [[C'est de la part de qui ?]] [[Un instant, s'il vous plaît.]]
- Leave a voicemail: [[Bonjour, c'est… Je vous appelle pour… Rappelez-moi au…]]
